articles.title: West Virginia's $12,000 Bet Pays Off: Digital Nomads Are Putting Down Roots
articles.summary: Ashley Eklin moved from Chicago to a town of 3,400 in West Virginia, lured by a $12,000 incentive. She's part of Ascend West Virginia, a privately funded program that's reversing population decline by attracting remote workers with cash and outdoor recreation.

articles.title: U.S. Slaps New Tariffs on Allies, Citing Forced Labor — Trading Partners Push Back
articles.summary: President Trump's latest tariffs, raising rates on goods from Australia, Japan, and others to 12.5%, are based on forced labor allegations. Australia's trade minister called them "completely unjustified," while China warned trade wars help no one.

articles.title: Burnham's First Week: Big Spending Pledges, But Where's the Money Coming From?
articles.summary: New UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham capped bus fares at £2, cut electricity VAT, and pledged £340m to end rough sleeping. But funding details remain vague, with experts questioning if the numbers add up.
